main_text.p: GALL. Nostra Gallia Narbonensis Corb (per apocopen) uocat: alij Durdo, alij Vergo, alij Corbau.
GERM. F. Ein kleiner Seerapp. (Rab quidem uel Rapp piscis fl. apud Saxones dictus, Capitoni fl. cognatus est.) Ein schwartzlachte Meerbrachsmen art.

Venetijs pictum hunc piscem, quondam Tincae marinae nomine accepi: sed falsò, ut admonuit Bellonius: qui uisa hac effigie statim Coruum mar. siue Carpam mar. id est, Coracinum esse pronunciauit. Colore magna ex parte nigricat tum corpore, tum pinnis: sed per latera fusco colori aliquid subuiride admixtum est. unde coloris nimirum ratione, Tincae mar. nomē (quod alij uulgò Merulae tribuunt, Romani etiam Phycidi Rondeletij, id est, Callariae Saluiani) imperitior aliquis ei adtribuit.
GERM. Ein andere figur deß obgenanten fischs/des schwartzeren.
Hæc quoq; Coracini species uidetur, colore ferè tantùm à precedenti differens: est enim candidior: reliqua uerò specie similis, oris nempe & caudæ, item latitudine, ac pinnis & aculeis in uentre.
GERM. Ein weyssere gattung deß obgenanten fischs.

page.notes: The two fish woodcuts are not transcribed as text. The word "PRAETER" at lower right is a catchword-type word at the foot. Some Fraktur words were read with [?] where uncertain; the Latin "Corb" in the first line is printed as "Corp" in the scan (per apocopen) and "Corbau" on the following line.
